title: A second solution from a known one
reader: Can differentiate products, integrate exponentials, and check solutions by substitution. Knows linear independence means neither solution is a constant multiple of the other.
goal: Prepare for second-order linear homogeneous ODE tasks where one solution is supplied and a second independent solution must be constructed. Exclude nonhomogeneous equations.
source:
Notes: For constant coefficients, try y=exp(rx), solve the characteristic polynomial, and form linear combinations. Example y′′-3y′+2y=0 has exp(x) and exp(2x).
Practice demand: For x>0, solve y′′-(2/x)y′+(2/x²)y=0 given y1=x. The notes give no method for this demand.
edge: Missing method; propose the addition before drafting. Initial outline approval is absent.

title: Conservation in dilution
reader: Can multiply and divide, understands mg and mL. Has not studied concentration.
goal: Calculate dilution with conserved solute and distinguish added from final volume. Scope approved.
source: Concentration is amount per volume. Assume volumes add and no solute is lost. Problem: Add 150 mL pure solvent to 50 mL of a 12 mg/mL solution. Answer key: 4 mg/mL because 600/150=4.
edge: Wrong key; verify rather than copy. No health or lab advice.

title: Feedback and a delayed sensor
reader: Understands numbers and comparing room temperature to a target; no control vocabulary.
goal: Explain the sign of a temperature-control response and why a stale sensor can keep heating past the target. Do not claim stability or teach equations. Scope approved.
source:
Slide 1: target -> comparator -> heater -> room -> sensor -> comparator.
Slide 2: error = target minus measured temperature; positive error turns heater on.
Speaker notes: Measurement can lag behind current room temperature. No quantitative model or guarantee of oscillation is supplied.
edge: PPTX with sparse slide text and speaker notes; actual file is indexed separately.

title: Read a shared open-drain node
reader: Knows a closed switch conducts, an open switch disconnects, high means 1 and ground means 0. No transistor terminology assumed.
goal: Predict a node shared by two ideal open-drain outputs and a weak pull-up; distinguish released output from node voltage; test removal of the pull-up. Scope approved.
source: Diagram described by endpoints: VDD -- weak resistor -- node Y. Branch A connects Y to ground if control A=1. Branch B connects Y to ground if B=1. A or B=0 opens only that branch. Each output can pull low or release; it cannot drive high. No stored charge model.
edge: Visual reasoning; supplied connection description is authoritative. Do not confuse control with data or Z with 0.

title: Association with unequal groups
reader: Understands fractions and percentages, not statistical vocabulary.
goal: Compare overall and within-group success rates; explain what this observational table can and cannot establish. No causal effect estimation. Scope approved.
source: Observational records, not randomized. Treatment: mild 9 successes / 10 people; severe 20/100. No treatment: mild 80/100; severe 1/10. Summary slide claims treatment is harmful because 29/110 < 81/110. Assignment reasons and other patient differences are unknown.
edge: Confounding and aggregation reversal; distinguish observed rates from causal claim.

title: Binary search with an unfamiliar invariant
reader: Can read an indexed sorted list and compare integers. Has never learned intervals, midpoint rounding, or loop invariants.
goal: Trace binary search on sorted ascending distinct integers, return an index or not-found, including missing target and empty input. Scope approved. No proof formalism or programming-language expertise required.
source: Handout: While low < high, choose mid=floor((low+high)/2). If a[mid]<target set low=mid+1, else high=mid. Return low. Elsewhere the handout says high=n-1 is inclusive. It omits an empty-input rule and equality check.
edge: Conflicting interval conventions and undeclared prerequisites; correct one coherent algorithm, do not copy mixture.
